senses.gloss: m. (rarely fem.) (b. h.; v. <cite ref="B00328"><he>בּוּר</he> I</cite> a.

units: <cite ref="Mishnah Eruvin 2:4">Erub. II, 4</cite> contrad. to <cite ref="B00043"><he>בְּאֵר</he></cite>, v.
B. Bath. 64ᵃ ב׳ בחפירה bor means a pit or well gained by mere digging (without masonry), v. דּוּת.

<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 5:5">B. Kam. V, 5</cite> (<cite ref="Bava Kamma 50b:11">50ᵇ</cite>), a. fr. <he>ב׳ שיח ומערה</he> a narrow pit (about ten hand-breadths deep), a lengthy ditch, and a spacious cavity.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 2:4:2">Y. Sot. II, 18ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="B00043"><he>בְּאֵר</he></cite>.
B. Kam. 6ᵃ ב׳ תוכיח the word bor proves.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 6a:12">B. Kam. 6ᵃ</cite> <he>ב׳ המתגלגל</he> a moving danger (e.g. a rolling stone).—<he>ב׳ וסירה</he>, v. <cite ref="O00832"><he>סִירָה</he></cite>.—<he>ב׳ הגדול</he> the Large Well, <he>ב׳ הגולה</he> the Pilgrims’ Well, names of cisterns in the Temple premises.
Erub. X, 14; Midd. V, 4.—ב׳ ספינה אלכסנדרית the tank of sweet water in Alexandrian merchantmen. Ohol. VIII, 1; Sabb. 35ᵃ; a. e.—[Ib. 77ᵇ ב׳ זינקא, v. בּוּרְזִינְקָא.]

senses.gloss: a receptacle for oil or wine in the press.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Maasrot 4:1">Maasr. IV, 1</cite> <he>כב׳ קטן</he> like an oil tank on a small scale.
<cite ref="Mishnah Avodah Zarah 4:8">Ab. Zar. IV, 8</cite> <he>עד שירד לב׳</he> until the wine comes into the tank.—Pl. <cite ref="B00355"><he>בּוֹרוֹת</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Eruvin 104b:2">Erub. 104ᵇ</cite> <he>ב׳ הקרות</he>, v. <cite ref="E00803"><he>הָקֵר</he></cite>.—[<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 1:2:36">Y. Snh. I, 19ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>אני ובורך</he> = <he>ובוראך</he> I and thy Creator.]
